name: Hana Ziegler

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary day at work involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and have just become junior manager of five payroll-correction clerks at a large shipping company. I spent many years fixing wage errors myself, so I know why a dock worker rings on payday, but I am still learning management budgets and am slower than the experienced managers. I have a bachelor’s degree. We compare clock records, shift premiums and the amount actually paid, then arrange a correction before the next payroll where we can.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How are you placed at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works at a library and our grown children have their own households. We have a small mortgage left and about a year of expenses saved. My salary is high for a junior manager because of my long service, and there are plenty of other payroll offices nearby, though I would check what they actually pay. I have never used AI at work; I trust a signed time record and a clerk who will ring the worker back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my clerks AI Plateau might copy a time entry faster, but it still cannot decide whether a night shift was paid at the right rate without checking the agreement. I would keep the worker’s call in the file.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect my post to be safe if the tool only saves a little copying. My partner’s library pay is regular, the mortgage is small and a year saved gives us room. I do not want to learn AI just to make a straightforward correction sound modern.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would continue the morning review of disputed shift premiums with the payroll clerk and call the worker before closing a case. If a small AI aid arrives in 2027, I would require the same signed timesheet and second clerk check. I would keep our ordinary mortgage payments and not count an untested pension figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about money and my job in this version. I would be furious if a copied figure left a night worker short on payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was the last disputed premium?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A dock worker completed three night shifts, but the payroll export paid only two. The missing night premium was visible on the signed time record. We corrected the wage before the worker’s next rent date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not let software settle it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Because someone has to check what the agreement says and tell the worker exactly when the money will arrive. I have never used AI for this work. I would rather have a clerk sign the correction than a screen announce that a case is closed.

say: A **copied time entry** still needs the shift agreement checked.
I would keep the **worker call** and signed timesheet in the case.
think: My **new manager post** looks safe under a small tool change.
A **year saved**, regular partner pay and small mortgage give room.
do: **Continue** morning shift-premium reviews with a clerk.
**Require** signed timesheets, worker calls and second checks after mild AI arrives.
feel: I feel **calm** about work but angry at short night wages.
S0.quote: We corrected the wage before the worker’s next rent date.
fieldNote: Her **never-used-AI** stance is explicit; she trusts signed records and a returned worker call.
A **year of savings** and higher long-service pay make mild change manageable.

steps.text: Continue morning disputed-premium review with payroll clerk
Require signed timesheets worker calls and second checks on wage corrections

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say stronger AI can compare clock entries and draft pay replies, and the company may hire fewer clerks. The union should see how many wages were actually corrected and how long workers waited. A cheap payroll run is not a success when someone misses rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think my new manager post could be combined with another team, even though I have years of correction experience. I am not fast with the management reports, and that is an easy weakness to point at. A year of savings and nearby offices give choices, but I do not know whether another employer would match my long-service rate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would bring ten delayed corrections to our union payroll committee and ask for an agreed time limit on getting missing wages to workers. I would not introduce an AI checker myself. If the company announces a merger, I would apply for posted payroll-supervisor roles only where verified pay after travel covers our mortgage and ordinary bills; I would leave only for a confirmed offer with an actual wage and rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a post I have only just grown into. I can search, but my team’s workers need their money before a management experiment is declared successful.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the ten cases show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One cleaner waited twelve days for an omitted weekend premium. Another worker had a wrong bank detail that took two payroll cycles to fix. I would show the time until workers received missing wages, not only the number of payroll tickets closed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not take a software course now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am not against a proved tool, but I do not want to spend unpaid evenings on one just because the company wants a lower headcount. If they show that it pays workers correctly and give paid time, I might reconsider. For now I would use the records I know.

say: **Automated payroll** should be judged by corrected wages and wait time.
I would use the **union committee** to set a correction deadline.
think: My **junior manager seat** could disappear in a merger.
A year saved helps, but another office may not match my **long-service pay**.
do: **Bring** ten delayed wage corrections to union payroll committee next month.
**Ask** for an agreed payment deadline for missing wages.
**Apply** to posted payroll-supervisor jobs only with verified mortgage-and-bill pay after travel.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible merger and protective of workers awaiting wages.
S1.quote: I would show the time until workers received missing wages, not only the number of payroll tickets closed.
fieldNote: She uses **paid-date evidence** through a union committee rather than promising an untested tool.
Her **year of savings** allows a search, but matching the long-service salary is uncertain.

steps.text: Bring ten delayed wage corrections to union payroll committee
Ask union committee for agreed deadline to pay missing wages
Apply to posted payroll roles only with verified pay after travel covering mortgage and bills
Leave only for confirmed offer with checked wage and rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company AGI by 2028 could calculate wages and reply to disputes before workers know who can reverse a wrong payment. I would demand written notice and a named person authorised to send a correction immediately.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think payroll offices may shrink sharply and my junior manager post might go. Another payroll desk or office manager writes and checks too, so 2028 AGI reaches those jobs. Dock loading remains physical until capable robots around 2031, but I have not done that work and cannot assume a vacancy or its pay. Our savings buy a search, not immunity.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the union committee for severance terms and a written rule giving a human authority to correct pay. I would check the actual mortgage balance and household bills with my partner, keeping our year of savings for a possible gap. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I would apply for posted local wage-administration work only after verifying the pay after travel and the hours; I would accept only a confirmed offer that covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious rather than helpless. Losing my higher wage would hurt, but we could search for a while and there are other firms; a vacancy is not a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you go onto a loading crew?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, not on the strength of a payroll title. A dock role has physical training and its own shifts, and robots arrive around 2031 in this picture. I would not put that wage into our plan before seeing an actual offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does immediate correction authority mean?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a dock worker’s night premium is missing, a named payroll officer can release the owed amount without waiting for a weekly meeting. A missing-wage appeal that arrives after a dock worker’s rent due date is not timely pay. The worker should know who can sign the correction.

say: **2028 AGI** needs human authority to reverse wrong pay.
I would demand written **notice and severance** before payroll cuts.
think: My **junior manager post** might go as payroll offices shrink.
Other wage desks face **2028 AGI**, while physical loading robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** union committee this week for severance and immediate correction authority.
**Check** mortgage and bills while preserving our year of savings for a gap.
**Apply** after a 2028 loss only to posted jobs with verified net pay and hours that cover bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing higher pay but able to fund a search.
S2.quote: A missing-wage appeal that arrives after a dock worker’s rent due date is not timely pay.
fieldNote: Her **higher salary and savings** limit immediate hardship but do not exempt a new manager post from desk automation.
She rejects **dock loading** as an assumed fallback; physical robots follow around 2031.

steps.text: Ask union for written severance and human authority to correct missing wages
Apply after loss to posted wage roles only with verified pay after travel and workable hours
Accept only confirmed offer that covers mortgage and bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets workers bargain for a real pay-appeal officer before a new payroll system arrives. The company should pay clerks to learn the actual agreement, not just offer a demonstration of an automated answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could become useful in wage grievance work because I know how a missed premium changes a household week. But reading agreements and preparing cases are thinking tasks too, so they face 2031 AGI. Loading crews face capable robots around 2034. At 63 I would need to see my actual retirement statement before deciding whether to keep working.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would ask the union for a paid grievance-observation place with an experienced representative. I would attend only if my payroll manager approves cover for my team and my full salary continues; I would not take unpaid evenings. I would apply after 2031 only for an advertised worker-pay appeals role with authority to release corrections and net wages that cover our mortgage; I would take it only on a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my new post, but I can learn a different duty while paid. A grievance title without the power to correct a wage would be decoration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the representative show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How to read the shift agreement against the clock record and how to let the worker explain a missing premium. I know the payroll form, but I have never represented someone in a grievance meeting. I would want the representative to tell me where my argument was weak.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Will the union guarantee a role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would be asking for an observation place first. An appeals job would still have to be advertised with real correction authority and pay I can live on.

say: A **five-year runway** should produce real pay appeals and paid agreement learning.
I would reject **demonstrations** that cannot fix missing wages.
think: Wage grievance preparation faces **2031 AGI**, even if I learn it.
At **63**, retirement income remains unverified and dock robots follow around 2034.
do: **Request** paid grievance observation with an experienced representative from 2027; attend only with payroll cover and full salary.
**Apply** after 2031 for advertised pay-appeal work only with release authority and mortgage-covering net wages.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the post but able to learn while paid.
S3.quote: I have never represented someone in a grievance meeting.
fieldNote: Her **grievance observation** is requested, not guaranteed; attendance needs cover, full salary and supervision.
A **pay-appeal role** is also exposed thinking work and requires a posting, authority and viable wages.

steps.text: Attend paid grievance observation only with payroll cover full salary and experienced representative
Apply after 2031 for posted appeal role only with wage-release authority and mortgage-covering pay
Take only confirmed offer with verified authority and wages

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union a decade is time to write pay-correction authority and notice terms into the agreement. I would not let a worker’s missing night premium become an acceptable error rate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 by 2036 and may want to retire, but I have not checked eligibility or the amount. Our year of savings and small mortgage give options; neither is a permanent income. Payroll and grievance reports face 2036 AGI, while physical dock work meets robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep checking signed time records and ask for a verified retirement-income statement, then compare income plus savings with our bills. I would add one hundred to savings only in months when both wages arrive in full, the mortgage and bills are paid and no large home repair is due. After 2036 I would keep paid work if verified retirement income plus savings cannot cover our costs; I would stop only after my partner and I see real figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about a distant job ending, but secure enough to check rather than guess. I would rather keep a year of cash than buy a promise about retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why cash with a small mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Because an office can close faster than a pension statement arrives. The extra hundred comes from full pay after our bills, not from emptying the year already saved. A large home repair would stop that transfer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make stopping possible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Verified income and savings that cover our bills without asking the grown children to pay. I have not read the actual terms yet. I will keep working if the numbers do not add up.

say: A **decade** should bring pay-correction authority and written notice.
I would refuse to normalise **missing night premiums** as an error rate.
think: At **68**, retirement eligibility and amount remain unverified.
Payroll and grievances face **2036 AGI**, with physical dock robots around 2039.
do: **Save** one hundred extra only after both full wages, mortgage and bills clear with no large home repair.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 unless verified retirement income plus savings cover costs.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about a distant closure but able to check real retirement figures.
S4.quote: The extra hundred comes from full pay after our bills, not from emptying the year already saved.
fieldNote: Her **new savings** come from full wages after bills, preserving the existing year-long cash reserve for an actual gap.
She makes no **retirement promise** without verified eligibility, income and household costs.

steps.text: Keep checking signed time records before correcting wages
Save hundred extra only with both full wages paid bills and no large home repair
Continue paid work after 2036 unless verified retirement income plus savings cover costs

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because payroll could shrink before a worker has a named person who can release missing pay. A written human correction rule, proper notice and a confirmed job with real wages if mine ends would help. We have savings, but I will not call an advertised post an offer.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the dock worker what the missing night premium meant before calling it a tiny payroll error. A wage correction after the rent date is a late wage. Someone should have the authority to fix it while the worker can still pay the bill.

headlineQuote: A wage correction after the rent date is a late wage.
portrait: **Hana, 58**, is a newly promoted junior payroll-corrections manager at a large shipping company.
Her **higher long-service pay**, library-worker partner, year-long reserve and many nearby offices support a small mortgage.
She has **never used AI** and relies on signed time records and returned worker calls.
She is **calm** under mild change, anxious about quick payroll cuts, and checks retirement terms before any decision.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink payroll before workers can reach someone authorised to correct missing wages.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, human wage-release authority and any confirmed replacement job with viable pay would help.
